task: relu_triton_kernel finite input words to typed grid refinement
standard: All original declared stages, dtypes and branches. Only explicitly registered numerical correspondence may be deferred; structural omissions remain blocking.
new_proved: Explicit signed/unsigned BitVec8/16/32/64 decoding with range bounds and source-word roundtrips.
All256 raw bool i8 words normalize via !=0 to unsigned i1 with exact zero/nonzero characterizations.
Signed extension and comparison agrees with decoded two's-complement nonnegativity; unsigned and normalized-bool comparisons are universally true in the audited routes.
Word comparison/select/source-width conversion result equals the already-proved typed result on the fully tagged decoded cell.
InputWords binds every active input offset; actual full ascending typed grid success is constructed with an independent initial-word result and complete frame.
Every written result is tagged fp32; an initially fp32-tagged output remains tagged, including its untouched tail.
A constructive logical input memory and a separate y!=x lemma make the logical alias/separate-output boundary explicit.

public_contract.structural_premise: InputWords equality of the complete tagged logical cell with explicit finite-word decoding at every offset below N; no successful-execution or result premise.
unclosed_numeric_callbacks: M.fromInt none on decoded signed source-width integers
M.fromNat none on decoded unsigned words or normalized unsigned i1 bool
M.literal none fp32 0 in the signed negative branch
public_contract.unused_inherited_parameters: cmp16/cmp32 occur in the existing backend parameterization but no integer/bool source operation or word result calls them.

memory_model.input_relation: For all o<N, initial.mem x o equals decodeCell encoding (words o), including the int/nat/bool tag. This rejects relying on mismatched-tag Cell.read defaults.
memory_model.output: Only pid0 writes fp32-tagged cells with offsets below both B and N when the modeled grid is nonempty. All other memory is the prelaunch memory.
memory_model.alias_policy: No x!=y hypothesis in the relation/grid theorem. withInputWords supplies decoded logical input memory; y!=x is explicitly required only to preserve a separately supplied output initialization. No physical alias correspondence is established.
memory_model.masked_lanes: No representation, finiteness or value condition is imposed for offsets outside N; their loads remain unspecified and their stores are masked.

structural_remaining.gap: Native loads to the explicit InputWords relation
structural_remaining.detail: Actual storage bytes, endianness, source-word assembly, tag correspondence, dtype dispatch and load-validity remain unproved. Finite-word decoding and bool normalization are now formal; defining decoded cells is not a native memory theorem.

Logical equal region names are permitted; shifted, misaligned or mixed-width physical byte views are not represented. The y!=x construction lemma preserves a supplied output region but does not prove fresh or separate empty_like allocation.

structural_remaining.gap: Native finite-width address, launch and error semantics
structural_remaining.detail: N, B, program IDs and element offsets still use Nat. Invalid block domains, zero-grid native behavior, pointer overflow and debug/sanitizer behavior are not closed.

structural_remaining.gap: Original dtype, host, compiler and execution scope
structural_remaining.detail: The prior fp64 value gap, four observed fp8 errors, noncanonical dtype families, native host/harness/module stages, compiler refinement and instruction interleavings remain open.

prior_original_structural_obligations_re.gap: Native fp64 value execution is unrepresented despite successful exact-source frontend generation; real is not relabeled as fp64.
The four observed fp8 errors need complete source-bound host/compiler semantics. e4nv/e5 fail comparison against int32 zero; fnuz admission failures are scoped to sm90, not all architectures.

Original dtype domain beyond the17 representative canonical signatures: shell int1/uint1 aliases, complex, quantized, packed and other dtypes need exact allocation, canonicalization and error behavior.
Integer width/byte decoding, bool raw-i8 normalization and tag correspondence are unproved. Decoded Int/Nat/Bool is not native byte or modular-arithmetic certification.
Native empty_like dtype/device/layout/freshness, accessor failures, input/output storage bounds and noncontiguous/offset views remain unbound; no missing runtime guards are invented.
Nat pid/offset/grid arithmetic requires finite-width native integer/address refinement, overflow/debug/error behavior and the valid block-size domain. Native zero-grid/zero-size behavior is unproved.
Native allocation overlap and instruction scheduling/compiler/runtime outcomes remain unproved; sequential logical execution alone is not native concurrency correctness.

Native host device/numel access, literal tensor creation, allocation, launch, return, dictionary operations and module execution are not bound to the logical primitives. Full native numerical harness completion is not claimed.

reduced_gap: RELU-S4 is refined by a proved finite-word decoding/comparison/normalization relation; native storage satisfying that relation remains a structural obligation.
